query: What signals suggest a support ticket will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: A clean categorical axis strongly plausible as a driver of resolution time (e.g. production_outage vs feature_request). All five samples map correctly to their source text (billing, auth, outage, feature, bug).

per_column.name: blocker_scope
per_column.rationale: Blast radius (single_user vs all_tenants) is a genuine, useful signal for effort/urgency. Sample mappings are mostly sound (all_tenants for the Acme outage, single_user for the session-drop). However 'team_or_account' appears to be a heavy default that may over-assert scope where text is thin (e.g. CS-0001, CS-0005 are arguably account-scoped but the read is defensible), slightly lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: business_impact
per_column.rationale: Impact severity is a reasonable new axis for prioritisation/resolution modelling. Sample values are warranted (financial_or_compliance_risk for the invoice with a finance deadline; operational_blockers for the outage). Uses 'not_present' appropriately for silent rows.

per_column.name: root_cause_clarity
per_column.rationale: Diagnostic readiness plausibly predicts resolution time and is a distinct axis. Most mappings are sound (suspected_by_customer_no_proof for the SSO guess; customer_provided_with_evidence for detailed bug reports). CS-0003 labelled customer_provided_with_evidence is borderline—the customer requests an RCA rather than providing one—so a modest groundedness deduction applies.

judge.rationale: All four added columns provide distinct, non-redundant categorical axes (issue nature, blast radius, business impact, diagnostic clarity) that each plausibly correlate with resolution time, directly serving the query. Values are largely well-grounded extractions/categorisations of the source text, with appropriate 'not_present' handling for silent rows. Minor concerns: a heavy default level in blocker_scope and one arguably over-confident root_cause_clarity label, but no clear hallucinations of invented facts.
